quests.instruction: Which shape has 4 corners and exactly two pairs of matching sides?
quests.hint: Look for the shape where the sides come in two matching pairs, not all four equal.
quests.explanation: A rectangle has exactly two pairs of matching sides: two long and two short.
quests.funFact: A rectangle always has two pairs of equal sides, even a very long, thin one.

quests.instruction: Which shape has 3 straight sides that always add up to a closed shape?
quests.hint: Look for the shape formed by connecting just three points together.
quests.explanation: Connecting any 3 points with straight lines always makes a closed triangle.
quests.funFact: A triangle is the simplest shape you can make using only straight lines.

quests.instruction: Which shape has no corners but looks stretched compared to a perfectly round shape?
quests.hint: Look for the shape that curves all around but isn't perfectly round.
quests.explanation: An oval curves all around with no corners, but it's stretched, unlike a perfectly round circle.
quests.funFact: Many eggs and footballs are shaped like ovals instead of perfect circles.

quests.instruction: Which shape has 4 sides, and cutting it exactly corner to corner makes two matching triangles?
quests.hint: Look for the shape where a diagonal line splits it into two equal triangle halves.
quests.explanation: Cutting a square from corner to corner always makes two matching triangles.
quests.funFact: This diagonal cut works because all four sides of a square are equal.

quests.instruction: Which shape has the same width no matter which direction you measure across it?
quests.hint: Look for the shape where every measurement across the middle comes out the same.
quests.explanation: A circle measures the same width across the middle no matter which direction you check.
quests.funFact: This equal-width property is unique to circles among common shapes.

quests.instruction: Which shape has 4 equal sides but its corners are not at the top-left, top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right?
quests.hint: Look for the shape whose corners point straight up, down, left, and right instead.
quests.explanation: A diamond's 4 equal sides meet at corners pointing up, down, left, and right, not at the usual box corners.
quests.funFact: Turning a square 45 degrees is exactly how you create a diamond shape.

quests.instruction: Which shape could be cut in half the short way to make two small squares?
quests.hint: Look for the shape that is exactly twice as long as it is wide.
quests.explanation: Some rectangles are exactly twice as long as they are wide, so cutting them in half makes two squares.
quests.funFact: Not every rectangle splits into squares — it depends on its exact length and width.

quests.instruction: Which shape has corners that always add up to the same total amount of turning?
quests.hint: Look for the shape with the fewest corners, where the angles always total the same amount.
quests.explanation: The three corners of any triangle always add up to the same total amount, no matter its size.
quests.funFact: This special rule about triangle corners is one of the first rules of shapes ever discovered.

quests.instruction: Which shape is a rectangle, but with the extra rule that all sides must match?
quests.hint: Look for the shape that fits the rectangle family, but is extra balanced.
quests.explanation: A square is actually a special rectangle where every side happens to be equal.
quests.funFact: That means every square is a rectangle, but not every rectangle is a square!

quests.instruction: Which shape is sometimes called a stretched circle by young learners?
quests.hint: Look for the shape that keeps the smooth curve of a circle but not the roundness.
quests.explanation: An oval keeps the smooth curved edge of a circle, but stretches it longer in one direction.
quests.funFact: Ovals have no corners at all, just like their circle cousin.

quests.instruction: Which shape has zero straight sides and zero corners, making it the roundest shape of all?
quests.hint: Look for the shape that is round on every single point of its edge.
quests.explanation: A circle has zero straight sides and zero corners, making it perfectly round all over.
quests.funFact: Wheels are shaped like circles so they roll smoothly without any bumps.

quests.instruction: Which shape shares its 4 equal sides with a square, but stands on a corner instead of a flat edge?
quests.hint: Look for the shape that seems tipped over compared to a plain box shape.
quests.explanation: A diamond has 4 equal sides like a square, but it balances on a corner instead of a flat edge.
quests.funFact: If you spin a square by 45 degrees, it turns into a diamond shape.

quests.instruction: Which shape needs the fewest straight lines to close up completely?
quests.hint: Look for the shape you cannot remove even a single side from.
quests.explanation: A triangle needs only 3 straight lines to close up completely.
quests.funFact: Two straight lines can never close up into a shape — you always need at least three.

quests.instruction: Which shape has 4 right-angle corners, just like a square, but a different side pattern?
quests.hint: Look for the shape with the same square corners as a square, but longer on two sides.
quests.explanation: A rectangle shares square corners with a square, but its sides are two different lengths instead of all equal.
quests.funFact: Both squares and rectangles always have four perfect right-angle corners.

quests.instruction: Which shape has 4 equal sides and would fit perfectly inside a picture frame that is just as tall as it is wide?
quests.hint: Look for the shape that would perfectly fill a frame shaped exactly like a box.
quests.explanation: A square fits perfectly in a frame that is equally tall and wide, since all its sides match.
quests.funFact: A square always has the same height and width, no matter how big it is.

quests.instruction: Which shape has a center point that is exactly the same distance from every edge point?
quests.hint: Look for the shape where the middle point never gets closer or farther from the edge.
quests.explanation: A circle's center is always the exact same distance from every point on its edge.
quests.funFact: This equal-distance rule is the actual definition mathematicians use for a circle.

quests.instruction: Which shape has two different curved measurements, one longer than the other?
quests.hint: Look for the shape that is a bit wider going one way than the other.
quests.explanation: An oval has one longer curved measurement and one shorter one, unlike a perfectly even circle.
quests.funFact: Ovals can be gently stretched circles, wider one way than the other.

quests.instruction: Which shape can be made by folding a square exactly in half along its corner-to-corner line?
quests.hint: Look for the shape you get from cutting a square along its diagonal.
quests.explanation: Folding or cutting a square along its diagonal line always makes two triangle halves.
quests.funFact: This is a handy trick — a square can always be split into two matching triangles.

quests.instruction: Which shape has 4 equal sides and its widest point exactly in the center, left to right?
quests.hint: Look for the shape that bulges out the most right in the middle.
quests.explanation: A diamond is widest exactly in the middle, between its top point and bottom point.
quests.funFact: This wide-middle look is what makes diamond shapes so easy to spot.

quests.instruction: Which shape has 4 sides, 4 corners, and could be described as the most balanced 4-sided shape?
quests.hint: Look for the shape with no side longer or shorter than any other.
quests.explanation: A square is the most balanced 4-sided shape because every side and angle matches.
quests.funFact: Because it's so balanced, a square is used in games like tic-tac-toe grids.

quests.instruction: Which shape has 4 sides and 4 corners, but is not as balanced as a square?
quests.hint: Look for the shape where two sides are clearly longer than the other two.
quests.explanation: A rectangle has 4 corners like a square, but its sides come in two unequal lengths.
quests.funFact: A rectangle can be stretched very long and thin while still keeping its four right angles.

quests.instruction: Which shape has no flat parts anywhere, making it impossible to stack neatly in a pile?
quests.hint: Look for the shape that would roll away instead of stacking flat.
quests.explanation: A circle has no flat sides, so round objects tend to roll instead of stack neatly.
quests.funFact: That's why coins are stacked flat side down, not rolled on their round edge.

quests.instruction: Which shape, when you add up its three corners, always gives the same total no matter its size?
quests.hint: Look for the shape with 3 corners and a very famous rule about their total.
quests.explanation: No matter how a triangle is shaped, its three corners always add up to the same fixed total.
quests.funFact: This is one of the very first rules children learn about triangles in geometry.

quests.instruction: Which shape looks like an egg lying on its side, with no corners at all?
quests.hint: Look for the shape that curves smoothly but isn't perfectly round like a ball.
quests.explanation: An oval looks like an egg on its side, curving smoothly with no corners at all.
quests.funFact: Egg shapes are ovals, though real eggs are usually a little more pointed on one end.

quests.instruction: Which shape has 4 equal sides, making every single side interchangeable with any other?
quests.hint: Look for the shape where you could swap any two sides and nothing would change.
quests.explanation: Because all 4 sides of a square are equal, you could swap them and the shape would look the same.
quests.funFact: This kind of matching is a big reason squares feel so neat and tidy.

quests.instruction: Which shape has 4 equal sides and points that line up like the top, bottom, left, and right of a compass?
quests.hint: Look for the shape whose four points spread out like north, south, east, and west.
quests.explanation: A diamond's four points spread out like the directions on a compass: up, down, left, and right.
quests.funFact: This four-point layout is what makes diamonds a favorite shape for kites.

quests.instruction: Which shape has 4 corners, and if you double one pair of sides you could reshape it into a square?
quests.hint: Look for the shape that would become a perfect square if its short sides grew to match the long ones.
quests.explanation: If a rectangle's shorter sides grew to match its longer sides, it would become a square.
quests.funFact: This shows how closely rectangles and squares are related in the shape family.

quests.instruction: Which shape has 3 sides and 3 corners, the smallest count of any straight-sided shape here?
quests.hint: Look for the shape with the fewest sides among all the choices.
quests.explanation: A triangle's 3 sides and 3 corners make it the simplest straight-sided shape in this game.
quests.funFact: Every other straight-sided shape you'll meet has more sides than a triangle.

quests.instruction: Which shape has an edge that never turns sharply, only curves gently the whole way around?
quests.hint: Look for the shape with absolutely no corners anywhere.
quests.explanation: A circle's edge curves gently the whole way around with no sharp turns anywhere.
quests.funFact: This total smoothness is what makes circles roll so perfectly.

quests.instruction: Which shape has 4 right-angle corners and two pairs of equal sides that are not all the same?
quests.hint: Look for the shape shaped like a stretched square, longer on two sides.
quests.explanation: A rectangle has 4 right-angle corners, with two pairs of equal sides that are not all four the same.
quests.funFact: You'll find rectangles everywhere — doors, books, phones, and windows.
